decisions.reason: Hosea's hearers knew this event, but it is mentioned nowhere else. Shalman may be a short form of Shalmaneser, the Assyrian king who later besieged Samaria (2 Kings 17:3-5), though no attack of his on a place called Beth-arbel is recorded. A king of Moab named Salamanu appears in a list of rulers who paid tribute to Assyria in Hosea's time, and he may have raided Gilead. Beth-arbel is usually placed at Arbela (modern Irbid) in Gilead, or at Arbel near the Sea of Galilee. None of these can be confirmed; what is clear is that the destruction was proverbial for its cruelty.

decisions.choice: a mother dashed to pieces with her children: the cruelty of ancient war
decisions.reason: Conquerors killed mothers and children alike (2 Kings 8:12; Psalm 137:9). Hosea warns that the same will happen in Samaria (14:1).

decisions.choice: an uproar among your people: the roar of war
decisions.reason: The word is the noise of a crowd or of battle (Amos 2:2). The preposition can mean "among" or "against"; the tumult of war will break out over the people.

decisions.choice: mothers ... with their children (B); Mothers and their children (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "a mother" stands for every mother. Balanced and Readable say "mothers".

decisions.choice: "Salmán", "Bet-arbel"
decisions.reason: Names found only here, spelled from the Hebrew in the Spanish way.

decisions.choice: "살만", "벧아벨"
decisions.reason: Spelled after Protestant convention for these names (cf. 살만에셀, 2 Kings 17:3); the shared footnote says the event is otherwise unknown.

decisions.choice: "San-man", "Bết-Ạt-bên"
decisions.reason: "San-man" is the terms note's form; "Bết-Ạt-bên" is new, built on the usual transliteration of "Beth-" and "Arbel".

decisions.choice: "Shalmani", "Beth-arbeli"
decisions.reason: New names, formed in the usual way (final -i after n and l; "Beth-" kept, as "Beth-aveni").

decisions.choice: o teu povo, as tuas fortalezas; Salmã, Bete-Arbel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the plural of verse 13 to the singular "your", Israel as one, so Portuguese turns back to "tu". The names are written as Portuguese spells their sounds, "Salmã" and "Bete-Arbel", like "Bete-Áven".

source.text: כָּ֗כָה עָשָׂ֤ה לָכֶם֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל מִפְּנֵ֖י רָעַ֣ת רָֽעַתְכֶ֑ם בַּשַּׁ֕חַר נִדְמֹ֥ה נִדְמָ֖ה מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus will do to you Bethel because of [the] evil of your evil; at the dawn utterly will be cut off [the] king of Israel.

en.L: Thus Bethel will do to you \q because of the evil of your evil; \q at dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
en.B: This is what Bethel will bring on you, \q because your wickedness is so great. \q At dawn the king of Israel will be completely cut off.
en.R: This is what Bethel will bring on you, \q because you have done so much evil. \q At sunrise the king of Israel will be completely destroyed.

es.L: Así {{plural_you:les|os}} hará Betel \q por la maldad de {{plural_you:su maldad|vuestra maldad}}; \q al amanecer será cortado por completo el rey de Israel.
es.B: Esto es lo que Betel traerá sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \q porque {{plural_you:su maldad|vuestra maldad}} es muy grande. \q Al amanecer el rey de Israel será destruido por completo.
es.R: Esto es lo que Betel traerá sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \q porque {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} mucho mal. \q Al salir el sol el rey de Israel será destruido por completo.

ko.L: 벧엘이 너희에게 이와 같이 할 것이다. \q 너희의 악 중의 악 때문이다. \q 새벽에 이스라엘의 왕이 아주 끊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 벧엘이 너희에게 이런 일을 가져올 것이다. \q 너희의 악이 너무나 크기 때문이다. \q 새벽에 이스라엘의 왕이 완전히 망할 것이다.
ko.R: 벧엘이 너희에게 이런 일을 가져올 것이다. \q 너희가 너무나 많은 악을 저질렀기 때문이다. \q 해가 뜰 무렵 이스라엘의 왕은 완전히 망할 것이다.

fr.L: Ainsi vous fera Béthel \q à cause de la méchanceté de votre méchanceté ; \q à l’aube, le roi d’Israël sera entièrement retranché.
fr.B: Voilà ce que Béthel vous attirera, \q parce que votre méchanceté est si grande. \q À l’aube, le roi d’Israël sera complètement retranché.
fr.R: Voilà ce que Béthel fera venir sur vous, \q parce que vous avez fait tant de mal. \q Au lever du soleil, le roi d’Israël sera complètement détruit.

vi.L: Bê-tên sẽ làm cho các ngươi như vậy \q vì điều ác của sự ác các ngươi; \q vào lúc rạng đông, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ bị diệt hoàn toàn.
vi.B: Đó là điều Bê-tên sẽ đem đến cho các ngươi, \q vì sự gian ác của các ngươi quá lớn. \q Vào lúc rạng đông, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ bị diệt hoàn toàn.
vi.R: Đó là điều Bê-tên sẽ đem đến cho các ngươi, \q vì các ngươi đã làm quá nhiều điều ác. \q Lúc mặt trời mọc, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ bị tiêu diệt hoàn toàn.

sw.L: Hivyo ndivyo Betheli itakavyowatendea \q kwa sababu ya uovu wa uovu wenu; \q alfajiri mfalme wa Israeli atakatiliwa mbali kabisa.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo Betheli itakavyowatendea, \q kwa sababu uovu wenu ni mkubwa mno. \q Alfajiri mfalme wa Israeli atakatiliwa mbali kabisa.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo Betheli itakavyowatendea, \q kwa sababu mmetenda maovu mengi sana. \q Jua linapochomoza, mfalme wa Israeli ataangamizwa kabisa.

pt.L: Assim fará Betel a vocês, \q por causa da maldade da maldade de vocês; \q ao amanhecer o rei de Israel será totalmente eliminado.
pt.B: É isto que Betel trará sobre vocês, \q porque a maldade de vocês é tão grande. \q Ao amanhecer o rei de Israel será completamente eliminado.
pt.R: É isto que Betel vai trazer sobre vocês, \q porque vocês fizeram muito mal. \q Ao nascer do sol o rei de Israel vai ser completamente destruído.

decisions.choice: Thus Bethel will do to you: Bethel brings the ruin on its worshipers
alternatives: So it will be done to you, Bethel
So I will do to you, house of Israel (the Greek)
decisions.reason: Bethel is most naturally the subject: the shrine they trusted will bring this ruin on them ("you" is plural, the people). It can also be read as an address to Bethel. The Greek translation (the Septuagint) has "So I will do to you, house of Israel".

decisions.choice: the evil of your evil: your great wickedness
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun makes it stronger: their wickedness is wickedness of the worst kind.

decisions.choice: at dawn: swiftly, at the first attack
decisions.reason: Dawn was the time of a sudden attack (Psalm 46:6; Judges 9:33). The end will come quickly, like the night ending.

decisions.choice: the king of Israel will be utterly cut off
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated for emphasis, the same verb as in verse 7. The northern kingdom's last king, Hoshea, was taken prisoner by Assyria before Samaria fell (2 Kings 17:4-6).

decisions.choice: At sunrise
decisions.reason: Readable says "sunrise" for "dawn".

decisions.choice: vocês; Betel
decisions.reason: The "you" is plural again, so Portuguese says "vocês". Here the text names Bethel itself, "Betel", not Bete-Áven.
